newsitem.title: CHINA: Shenzhen B shares down at noon, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Shenzhen B shares down at noon, trade thin.

text.p: Shenzhen's hard currency B share index was slightly lower in thin trade at midday on Wednesday as market sentiment remained poor, brokers said.
The index lost 0.33 point or 0.26 percent to 129.37 on reduced turnover of HK$5.4 million against Tuesday morning's HK$9.5 million.
The domestic A share index gained 4.54 points or 1.14 percent to 401.69, powered by market talk that Beijing may further ease credit controls by lowering bank reserve requirements, brokers said.
Turnover on the A share market was 1.97 billion yuan in the morning session.
"B share investors lack confidence," a broker at China Southern Securities Co said.
"Investors are still taking a wait-and-see attitude," said an analyst at China Guotai Securities. "The (B share) index is expected to fall further and is looking for short-term support."
Beverage maker Shenzhen Shenbao Industrial Co was the biggest loser on the B share market in the morning, sliding HK$0.24 or 7.41 percent to HK$3.00.
Bengang Steel was the most actively traded issue on volume of 501,500 shares. It lost HK$0.01 to HK$1.99 and remained well below its recent offer price of HK$2.38.
Shenzhen Development Bank, the A share market leader, was among the most actively traded counters, gaining 0.55 yuan to 34.75 yuan on volume of 2.5 million shares.
